name: NVIDIA
role: Designs the dominant AI GPUs; the hub of the whole supply chain.

name: AMD
role: Designs GPUs and CPUs; the main GPU alternative.

name: Intel
role: Designs CPUs and runs its own fabs; turnaround underway, now part-owned by the US government.

name: Broadcom
role: Designs custom AI accelerators and networking silicon; builds Google's TPUs.

name: Marvell Technology
role: Custom AI silicon and interconnect; data center is ~75% of revenue.

name: Arm Holdings
role: Licenses the CPU IP most AI systems are built on; ~97% gross margin.

name: TSMC
role: Fabricates and packages nearly all leading-edge AI silicon.

name: Samsung
role: HBM memory (tertiary supplier) and a foundry competitor.

name: SK Hynix
role: NVIDIA's primary HBM supplier; ~62% HBM share.

name: Micron
role: US-based HBM supplier; share growing off a small base.

name: ASML
role: Sole maker of EUV lithography machines; the hardest chokepoint in the chain.

name: Applied Materials
role: Wafer-fabrication and deposition equipment.

name: Dell
role: Integrates chips into finished servers and racks.

name: Supermicro
role: Server and rack integration for AI clusters.

name: Arista
role: Networking switches that connect racks; runs on Broadcom silicon.

name: Microsoft
role: Hyperscaler and OpenAI's original backer; building its own Maia chips.

name: Amazon
role: Hyperscaler and Anthropic's core partner; building Trainium chips.

name: Google
role: Hyperscaler and model lab; designs its own TPUs via Broadcom.

name: Oracle
role: Cloud provider anchoring Stargate.

name: Meta
role: Hyperscaler and open-model leader; multi-gigawatt superclusters.

name: CoreWeave
role: Neocloud; NVIDIA holds an equity stake and it buys NVIDIA GPUs.

name: OpenAI
role: The largest single buyer of compute.

name: Anthropic
role: Frontier lab with a multi-vendor chip strategy.

name: xAI
role: Frontier lab; built the Colossus cluster fast.

name: SoftBank
role: Mega-investor funding OpenAI, Stargate, and power buildout.

name: HUMAIN
role: Saudi Arabia's PIF-backed national AI champion.

name: G42
role: UAE's state-linked AI firm.

name: US Government
role: Sets chip export policy; now an Intel shareholder.

name: Shin-Etsu
role: World's largest silicon-wafer maker; also photoresists and photomask blanks.

name: SUMCO
role: Pure-play silicon-wafer maker; polished and epitaxial 300mm wafers.

name: Linde
role: World's largest industrial-gases company; ultra-high-purity gases piped on-site into fabs.

name: Lam Research
role: Etch and deposition equipment; the memory makers' indispensable tool vendor.

name: KLA
role: Process-control and yield-management leader; inspection and metrology for every leading fab.

name: Tokyo Electron
role: Coater/developer leader, plus etch and deposition; a top-three tool vendor.

name: ASE Technology
role: World's largest OSAT; advanced packaging and test for fabless chipmakers.

name: Amkor
role: Largest US-headquartered OSAT; ~$12B advanced-packaging campus rising in Peoria, Arizona.

name: Vertiv
role: Data-center power and cooling infrastructure; partnered with NVIDIA on AI-factory designs.

name: Eaton
role: Intelligent power management; UPS and electrical distribution for data centers.

name: Nebius
role: Neocloud GPU provider spun out of Yandex; $17.4B Microsoft capacity deal.

name: Vistra Corp.
role: Independent power producer supplying electricity to homes and businesses across the US; its nuclear and gas fleet feeds the AI data-center power rush.

name: Talen Energy Corp
role: Independent power producer in PJM markets; its Susquehanna nuclear plant powers a large data-center campus next door.

name: NRG Energy, Inc.
role: Retail electricity provider and power plant operator; building new gas-fired generation aimed at data-center load growth.

name: GE Vernova Inc.
role: Designs and builds gas turbines, wind turbines, and grid equipment; its turbines are the hardware inside new AI-era power plants.

name: Bloom Energy Corp
role: Manufactures solid-oxide fuel-cell ‘Energy Servers’ that generate power on-site; data centers use them to get power without waiting on grid upgrades.

name: Quanta Services, Inc.
role: Builds and maintains electric grid, power generation, and communications infrastructure; a core contractor for AI data-center power hookups.

name: Comfort Systems USA, Inc.
role: Installs and services HVAC, electrical, and plumbing systems in commercial buildings; a direct beneficiary of the data-center construction boom.

name: QUALCOMM Incorporated
role: Designs Snapdragon mobile chips, 5G modems and wireless IP; its platforms run on-device AI in phones, PCs and cars.

name: Teradyne, Inc.
role: Builds automated test equipment that validates chips and electronics — including AI accelerators — before they ship.

name: Amcor plc
role: Makes flexible and rigid consumer packaging for food, beverage, healthcare and personal-care brands.

name: Sandisk Corporation
role: Makes NAND flash memory and solid-state storage for phones, PCs, and data centers; spun out of Western Digital in February 2025.

name: Seagate Technology Holdings plc
role: Builds hard-disk drives, including high-capacity nearline drives used by cloud data centers to store AI-era data.

name: Western Digital Corporation
role: Builds hard-disk drives and storage platforms for cloud, client, and consumer markets; its former flash business is now Sandisk.

name: IREN Limited
role: Bitcoin miner converting its low-cost power footprint into AI cloud data centers, with ~$16.6B of contracted revenue and lease value across AI cloud and bitcoin mining customers.

name: TeraWulf Inc.
role: Bitcoin miner pivoting to AI data centers, leasing large-scale HPC capacity to tenants under long-term contracts from its New York campuses.

name: Hut 8 Corp.
role: Bitcoin miner turned energy-infrastructure platform, developing AI data center campuses (River Bend and Beacon Point) backed by multi-billion-dollar project financing.

name: Galaxy Digital Inc.
role: Digital-asset financial services firm (trading, lending, asset management) expanding into AI data centers, leasing data hall capacity from its Helios campus in Texas.

name: Applied Digital Corporation
role: Designer, builder and operator of large-scale AI data center campuses in North Dakota, with long-term hyperscale leases including a $7.5B 15-year deal.

name: Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd
role: Designs high-speed connectivity chips and active electrical cables that move data between GPUs and switches inside AI clusters.

name: Astera Labs, Inc.
role: Makes PCIe/CXL retimers and memory-connectivity chips that keep processors, accelerators, and memory in sync in AI servers.

name: Cisco Systems, Inc.
role: The incumbent enterprise-networking giant; its switches, routers, and security gear now ride AI data-center buildouts.

name: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co
role: Provides servers, storage, and networking (now including Juniper) for enterprise and AI data centers.

name: Ciena Corporation
role: Builds optical networking systems that carry massive data flows between and within AI data centers.

name: Coherent Corp.
role: Makes lasers, optical components and transceivers for AI datacenters and industrial systems.

name: Lumentum Holdings Inc.
role: Makes lasers, optical components and transceivers for AI datacenter connectivity and telecom networks.

name: Fabrinet
role: Contract manufacturer that builds optical transceivers and precision components for datacenter and telecom OEMs.

name: Applied Optoelectronics, Inc.
role: Designs and manufactures optical transceivers for AI datacenters and cable broadband networks.

name: POET Technologies Inc.
role: Develops photonic integrated circuits and optical engines for AI datacenter interconnects; still pre-revenue.

name: Palantir Technologies Inc.
role: Data analytics and AI software for government and enterprise; its Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP) turns operational data into decisions.

name: ServiceNow, Inc.
role: Cloud workflow-automation platform for enterprise IT and operations, layering AI agents across service workflows.

name: Salesforce, Inc.
role: Cloud CRM and customer-data platform; Agentforce brings AI agents to sales, service, and marketing workflows.

name: Snowflake Inc.
role: Cloud data warehouse sold on consumption pricing; AI and LLM data products run directly on customer data in its platform.

name: MongoDB, Inc.
role: Document database for developers; Atlas, its managed cloud database, underpins data layers for many AI applications.

name: Datadog, Inc.
role: Cloud monitoring and observability platform; watches the infrastructure that AI workloads run on.

name: AppLovin Corporation
role: AI-driven mobile advertising platform; its machine-learning ad engine places ads across app inventory at scale.

name: Atlassian Corporation
role: Team collaboration software (Jira, Confluence); AI assistants such as Rovo work across its Teamwork Graph.

name: Twilio Inc.
role: Cloud communications platform (voice, messaging, and email APIs) that enterprises use to build AI-driven customer engagement.

name: CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc.
role: AI-native cybersecurity platform (Falcon) protecting endpoints, cloud workloads, and identity through SaaS subscriptions.

name: Palo Alto Networks, Inc.
role: Cybersecurity platform company consolidating enterprise network, cloud, and AI security on its Strata, Prisma, and Cortex platforms.

name: Zscaler, Inc.
role: Cloud-native zero-trust security platform securing users, workloads, and AI applications without traditional firewalls.

name: Cloudflare, Inc.
role: Global connectivity cloud (edge network, CDN, and zero-trust security) increasingly used to run AI inference at the edge.

name: SentinelOne, Inc.
role: AI-powered endpoint and cloud security platform (Singularity) competing on autonomous threat detection and response.

name: Fortinet, Inc.
role: Network-security appliance and software vendor converging networking and security for enterprises and AI data centers.

name: Okta, Inc.
role: Identity and access management platform for workforce and customer identity, securing logins and access in the AI era.
